title: Why Did XOM, CVX, MPC Stocks Surge To 52-Week Highs Today? - Stocktwits
content: Shares of energy companies Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM), Chevron Corp. (CVX), and Marathon Petroleum Corp. (MPC) surged to annual highs on Monday as oil prices rallied amid growing geopolitical tensions. Brent crude prices touched nearly $110 a barrel on Monday as tensions in the Middle East continued to ratchet up. A series of recent escalations, including attacks on commercial ships near the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi missile strikes on Saudi Arabia, and Ukraine’s strike on a Russian refinery, stoked fears about a further constraint in fuel supplies, sending prices higher. Worries continued despite the U.S. government’s efforts to curtail rising prices, including planned fuel releases and changes to U.S. sanctions on Russian imported fuel. Since the U.S.-Iran war began in February, energy prices have been climbing steadily, boosting energy companies. As per Koyfin data, energy stocks have outperformed the S&P 500 by a significant margin in 2026. Exxon Mobil, Chevron, and Marathon Petroleum shares surged to 52-week highs on Monday before closing lower amid the steep climb in oil prices. XOM stock hit an annual high of $179.30 during trading hours on Monday before closing about 0.4% down. CVX stock surged to a 52-week high of $225.67, but ended the session 0.28% lower. MPC stock rallied to a 52-week high of $493.98 during regular trading, but finished the day nearly 1% down. Retail sentiment around XOM, CVX and MPC stocks was ‘bullish’ at the time of writing on Stocktwits. XOM stock has gained more than 48% year-to-date, while CVX and MPC stocks have surged more than 47% and 200%, respectively. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Retail investors in Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) are floating multibillion-dollar buyout scenarios and steep share-price gains after CEO Angelos Stergiou marked the company’s 15th anniversary with a post about its “next chapter.” SLS stock jumped 5% on Monday to $10.49, snapping three straight losing sessions. In his LinkedIn post, Stergiou reflected on Sellas’ growth from a private startup into a public biotech advancing investigational cancer treatments GPS and SLS009. “Reaching 15 years isn't just about celebrating our history; it is about stepping into our next chapter with even greater focus, drive, and resolve,” he said. He acknowledged past setbacks and thanked shareholders, employees and trial participants, while reaffirming the company’s commitment to patients. “Our mission remains deeply personal, and our promise to the patients we aim to serve is steadfast. We look forward, God willing, to the best chapters that are still to be written with GPS and SLS009,” he added. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for SLS slipped to ‘bearish’ from ‘bullish’ levels a day ago amid a 258% jump in 24-hour message volumes. One user said: “My opinion, Dr. Stergiou’s message was a master-class at reassuring EVERYONE that all is well.” A user also floated a minimum $40 billion valuation. Another user argued for a $50 billion valuation, calling a $247-per-share figure. A separate user proposed a $120 billion buyout scenario and also predicted a share price of $540-plus. Across bullish share-price predictions, including scenarios tied to clinical results, targets ranged from $100 to over $540. Discussing buyout news in case of favorable data, one user said: “If BO news post good data then there’s no stopping this beast (really no explanation required as it could go full berserker mode).” BO means buyout. Another user challenged the lofty valuations and said: “I will be so glad to get out of this ticker when it hits $15 again.” The CEO’s message comes as investors have been searching for potential deal signals in recent months. In June, a filing disclosed changes to executive severance arrangements, including lump-sum payment provisions for Stergiou. For CFO John Burns and chief development officer Dragan Cicic, qualifying departures within one month before or one year after a change of control would trigger 15 months of salary, the annual target bonus, up to 18 months of health-coverage reimbursements and full vesting of unvested equity. Sellas’ conference plans have provided another talking point. The company is listed at Booth 138, with a 20-by-30-foot space, for the Dec.12- Dec.15 American Society of Hematology (ASH) meeting in New Orleans. Major exhibitors include Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, AbbVie and Bristol Myers Squibb. The booth size has fueled speculation about a partnership or acquisition. Currently, investors are awaiting data from Sellas’ two lead programs. The Phase 3 Regal trial is testing GPS, an immunotherapy targeting WT1, in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) patients who achieved a second complete remission following salvage treatment. Its final-analysis process is triggered by 80 deaths. Sellas reported 78 events as of May 11. Reaching 80 precedes database lock, data review and analysis before results are disclosed. The company also expects fourth-quarter topline data from its 80-patient Phase 2 SLS009 study in newly diagnosed AML, including patients with early resistance to azacitidine and venetoclax. SLS009 is also being explored in pancreatic cancer. Preclinical findings from last month showed 17.9% apoptosis (programmed cell death) in a patient-derived tumor model resistant to Daraxonrasib, versus 2.8% with Daraxonrasib alone. Combining the drugs raised apoptosis to 36.5% and necrosis to 30.6%. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. U.S. stock futures climbed into positive territory late Monday as technology stocks rebounded after a sharp selloff last week. Meanwhile, markets are keenly watching the third-quarter (Q3) earnings season unfold, with about 70 S&P 500 companies slated to report earnings this week. As of 11:13 p.m. EDT, Dow futures were up about 0.25%, while the S&P 500 futures gained 0.21% and the Nasdaq-100 futures climbed 0.15%. On Monday, the three benchmark indexes closed mixed. The Nasdaq Composite led the climb, adding more than 290 points to close 1.11% higher. The S&P 500 climbed 0.41% at close, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.07%. Technology and AI stocks were top of mind for markets on Monday as the sector reversed last week's steep selloff. Chip stocks led the climb on Monday. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) closed up nearly 2%, while the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) closed up 1.61%. Nvidia Corp. (NVDA), Micron Technology Inc. (MU) and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) all ended the session in green. The run comes ahead of vital Q3 results that will follow this week, which are likely to set the tone for the trajectory of technology shares. “Tech earnings are key this week. Fundamentals are unchanged, but given fragile price action, we turn neutral [on] risk assets and stay neutral duration,” Ajay Rajadhyaksha, global chairman of research at Barclays, said in a note, according to CNBC. Katie Stockton, founder of Fairlead Strategies, reportedly said in a note on Monday that the week will be crucial for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, which need to hold support, while noting that a hold is possible amid widespread, short-term oversold conditions. Meta Platforms (META) and Tesla (TSLA) are due to report Q3 results later this week, while multiple other semiconductor and technology companies, including Lam Research (LRCX) and Texas Instruments (TXN), will also post their results. AI-related power companies Bloom Energy (BE) and Valero Energy (VLO), along with big entertainment companies including Netflix Inc. (NFLX), will also announce their quarterly results. Meanwhile, rising oil prices amid growing geopolitical uncertainty have put downward pressure on markets. Brent crude futures expiring in December were trading at $109.88 a barrel, up about 0.3%, while WTI crude futures expiring in November traded at $103.64 per barrel. Economist Peter Schiff said in a post on X, “Oil rose another 2.5% today. It's almost $104. If you think gas prices are high now, just wait until after the midterms when Trump has to turn off the spigots from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to keep it from running dry. Oil could hit $150, sending gas prices to record highs.” Trump Media & Technology Group Corp. (DJT): Shares of the president’s media company were in focus late Monday after the stock slipped 8%, its worst single-day drop since February, as President Donald Trump’s approval rating hit a record low. Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN): The company’s stock surged nearly 5% at close on Monday and continued to climb higher overnight after Morgan Stanley raised its price target and named it a ‘Top Pick.’ Cerebras Systems Inc. (CBRS): The AI hardware and supercomputing company was on the retail radar after shares slipped more than 5% on Monday, extending a broader selloff in the sector from last week. CoreWeave Inc. (CRWV): Shares of the neocloud company fell more than 1% in overnight trading late Monday, putting it on track for a third week of declines amid a selloff in software names. Among ETFs tracking benchmark indexes, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) all climbed overnight. Meanwhile, U.S. long-dated Treasury yields continued above 5%. At the time of writing, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield was 5.138%, and the 30-year Treasury yield was 5.473%. The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) was up 0.09% amid ‘bullish’ sentiment. Asian markets opened lower on Tuesday, with South Korea's KOSPI, Japan’s Nikkei 225, China’s SSE Composite and Australian stocks all trading lower at the time of writing. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. Shares of Broadcom, Inc. (AVGO) reversed overnight losses to edge up 0.3% late Monday as a 10-year cloud agreement with NTT Docomo did little to ease retail skepticism, with traders seeking a recovery catalyst after CEO Hock Tan’s AI “casino” remarks. AVGO stock rose nearly 2% on Monday to close at $334.59, snapping three straight sessions of losses. Broadcom extended its 2019 deal with Docomo, in which the companies will align their long-term tech roadmaps to advance the private cloud underpinning the Japanese telecom operator’s digital services. The company called it Broadcom Japan’s first “comprehensive” 10-year agreement covering VMware software licenses, technical assistance and maintenance support. Financial terms were not disclosed. VMware Cloud Foundation will be at the core of the infrastructure. The deal targets three priorities: keeping services available during system upgrades, strengthening security and resilience, and accelerating the delivery of new services. Docomo will use the platform to expand capacity and manage traffic spikes, improve security patching and anomaly detection, and run virtual machines and containers on a common platform. Automation across development, testing and releases will help shorten the time needed to introduce new features. The companies also plan to expand AI-driven operations and prepare the infrastructure for future developments, including 6G and IOWN. The agreement comes a week after Tan’s comments at a Singapore panel, where he called capital the biggest constraint on further AI development as Broadcom works through wafer and memory shortages. “A lot of investors have no clue what they're investing in, but set very extreme expectations, only to find out that it's almost like they are in a casino gambling,” Tan said when asked about cheaper AI models, Reuters noted. His remarks addressed investment into the broader AI sector. Tan also acknowledged that Anthropic and OpenAI had shown an ability to generate significant revenue from their latest models deployed for AI personal assistants. SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk also subsequently responded, saying, “No crying in the casino,” weighing in on Tan’s concerns about speculative AI investments. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for AVGO slipped to ‘extremely bearish’ at 24/100 — its lowest levels in nearly 18 months — from ‘bearish’ levels a day ago amid a 300% surge in 24-hour message volumes. Retail interest in the stock has been rising, with the ticker’s watcher base up 8% over the past three months. One user said, “The biggest problem with this stock is lack Catalysts from Broadcom, the last news was on Oct 13 for VMware HyperArmor. But nothing after it.”  Another user said, “Each time they beat earnings and revenue estimates. Yet here we are down 15% in that time frame.” A separate user said, “trash news! Still headed lower,” shortly after the Docomo agreement. Other traders were still looking for a bounce. Another user said, “when we sell off early into the session typically we see a nice reversal in overnight session into premarket.” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. (CRWV) shares fell nearly 2% in overnight trading late Monday, putting it on track for a third week of declines amid a selloff in software names. However, Cathie Wood's ARK Investment purchased 132,498 shares of the company on Monday despite the selloff. The asset manager’s ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) bought 102,280 CRWV shares on Monday for $6.3 million, according to its website. The firm also bought 30,218 shares of CRWV for $1.8 million through the ARK Next Generation Technology ETF (ARKW). The purchase comes as Wall Street and Main Street remain concerned about the company’s ballooning debt levels. CoreWeave reported $35.6 billion in total debt as of June 30, while its second-quarter net interest expense rose to $640 million from $267 million a year earlier. Research and advisory firm Gartner recently said in a report that artificial intelligence infrastructure investments are in danger as concerns over bloated AI capex mount. The firm said that as the commercial duopoly for primary frontier models consolidates around Anthropic and OpenAI, the cash flows to meet that massive computing asset base from neoclouds are not scaling proportionally with upfront costs. Meanwhile, major Wall Street analysts are also taking opposing stances on CoreWeave. MoffettNathanson and BNP Paribas lowered their price targets on CoreWeave, while Goldman Sachs took a more positive outlook. MoffettNathanson slashed CRWV stock’s target to $89 from $107 and kept a ‘Neutral’ rating on the shares, citing its “staggering financial obligations.” BNP Paribas also cut its price target on CoreWeave to $117 from $169 and maintained an ‘Outperform’ rating, according to The Fly. The firm said that it sees a continued deterioration in investor confidence amid its debt obligations. While higher financing costs could contain the company's ability to fund future growth, the shares are "seemingly discounting some liquidity concerns," the analyst reportedly said in a research note. However, Goldman Sachs upgraded the stock to ‘Buy’ from ‘Neutral’ and set a price target of $106, implying upside of more than 73% from its last close. The firm said ongoing volatility in the credit market raises questions about whether CoreWeave can finance its next phase of growth, and at what pace. However, Goldman also said the ongoing debate over demand for frontier vs. off-frontier intelligence, and CoreWeave's annual recurring revenue per megawatt and unlevered internal rate of return, are "biased to the upside" over the next 24 months because of tight supply. The analyst also said that CoreWeave is differentiated from other neoclouds. Last week, Dan Ives, Yorkville Ives partner and senior managing director analyst, said in an interview that the recent sell-off was an overreaction, as the broader AI demand story remains intact. “I'm not saying there's not some issues in terms as rates go higher. But given the demand, given backlog, I think this is ultimately a false narrative,” he said, while also highlighting that the sharp drop has created an opportunity for investors. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for CRWV stock was ‘extremely bullish,’ even as message volumes surged 938% over 24 hours, according to platform data. One user said, “$CRWV $NBIS are moving in tandem.. absolutely nothing to see here…” The user added, “When the wrestling match ends, these are going straight up, meanwhile, you or I have zero say in it.” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. EyePoint Pharmaceuticals (EYPT), CoreWeave (CRWV) and Eos Energy Enterprises (EOSE) hit fresh 52-week lows Monday as a failed drug trial, debt refinancing concerns, and weaker full-year revenue expectations weighed on the stocks. EyePoint stock crashed 85%, while CoreWeave and Eos Energy stocks dropped 0.4% and 0.5%, respectively. EyePoint Pharmaceuticals stock crashed to a record low of $0.4 after the company reported disappointing results from LUCIA, its second pivotal Phase 3 study of DURAVYU, an experimental treatment for wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD). The drug failed to show that it worked as well as aflibercept in protecting vision at Weeks 52 and 56, hurting its chances of approval for the eye condition. The setback prompted the company to lay off 53% of its workforce, with the restructuring expected to bring $30 million in annualized savings and incur about $9 million in severance expenses. EyePoint reported roughly $118 million in cash and equivalents as of Sept. 30 and plans to concentrate its remaining resources on Phase 3 studies of DURAVYU for diabetic macular edema (DME). However, on Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock flipped to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bearish’. CoreWeave stock fell to a new annual low of $59.25 as analysts cut price targets amid concerns about its debt obligations and reliance on external funding. BNP Paribas lowered its price target to $117 from $169 while retaining an ‘Outperform’ rating. MoffettNathanson cut its target to $89 from $107 and maintained a ‘Neutral’ rating. The analysts highlighted the potential consequences of weaker investor confidence and expensive financing. CoreWeave needs capital to expand its data center infrastructure and support growing demand for computing capacity. Higher borrowing costs and limited access to capital markets could complicate its expansion plans and weigh on shareholder returns. Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bullish’. Eos Energy Enterprises stock touched a two-year low of $1.72 despite reporting preliminary third-quarter (Q3) revenue of $82 million to $83 million, a sequential growth of 19% to 21%. However, investors focused on the company’s expectation that 2026 revenue would land in the lower half of its previously announced $300 million to $350 million range. The updated outlook follows an earlier reduction in the company's revenue forecast in August. Eos has recorded eight consecutive quarters of improving gross margins, but its margins remain deeply negative as it works to increase production and improve manufacturing efficiency at its Thorn Hill facility. Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘bearish’. So far this year, EYPT, CRWV and EOSE stocks have declined between 14% and 97%. title: Exxon (XOM) shuts catalytic reformer at Joliet, Illinois refinery (275k BPD) - Newsquawk
content: Exxon (XOM) shuts catalytic reformer at Joliet, Illinois refinery (275k BPD) Unplanned unit outages at large US refineries follow a well-worn template: the initial read-through runs through product cracks rather than crude, with gasoline and distillate spreads in the relevant PADD tightening while the affected complex's crude demand dips at the margin. A catalytic reformer matters specifically because it supplies high-octane gasoline blendstock and the hydrogen that feeds desulphurisation units, so a prolonged outage can constrain finished gasoline output even where crude distillation keeps running. The size of the site puts it among the larger plants in the Midwest system, meaning sustained downtime has historically shown up in regional basis and PADD II product supply rather than in national balances. The distinctions that separate a non-event from a crack rally are duration and whether the shutdown is planned maintenance or a forced outage, and whether co-located units are affected. The follow-ons are company confirmation of cause and expected restart, any knock-on to crude runs, and weekly inventory data for the region. For the equity, single-unit downtime at an integrated major has rarely moved the stock beyond the session, the earnings exposure sitting in downstream margins rather than group results. As megacap technology names swung hard through a crowded run of quarterly updates, money leaned toward the oil majors, and the largest integrated producer on the American market drew a fresh bid alongside firmer barrels. Trading desks framed the stretch as a search for ballast while the technology complex churned. Crude sits at the heart of the energy complex, so a sharp climb in the barrel tends to ripple quickly through the producers that pull it from the ground. When oil firms, the output each field delivers fetches a stronger price, lifting the cash a large producer can generate without any change to the barrels it lifts. That leverage to the barrel is a defining feature of the energy arena. A steady climb in crude can lift the reported earnings of an upstream producer faster than the move in oil itself, because the cost of lifting each barrel stays broadly fixed while the sale price rises. The upstream arm finds and produces crude oil and natural gas across a spread of regions, feeding the barrels that anchor the group's earnings. The downstream arm refines that crude into gasoline, diesel, jet fuel and other products, while the chemical arm converts feedstocks into plastics and specialty materials sold into countless end markets. This integrated design is the hallmark of the business. When crude is strong, the upstream arm drives earnings; when margins on refined fuels widen, the downstream arm carries more weight; and the chemical arm adds a thread tied to broad industrial demand. An integrated energy group captures value at several stages of the chain at after, and that breadth tends to smooth the swings that buffet a pure upstream producer. When crude slides, cheaper feedstock can lift refining and chemical margins, so the downstream arms can cushion a softer barrel, lending the whole group a steadier character across the cycle. That balance cuts the other way too. When crude climbs sharply, as it did this week, the upstream arm shines while refining faces costlier input, yet the combined base still leans toward the firmer barrel. Readers following Oil and Gas Stocks can place this update within its wider category. The deepwater development has moved from early finds to steady production, adding a large and growing stream of barrels to the group's base. The Guyana play matters because its barrels come at a competitive cost and from a region where the group holds a commanding position alongside its partners. That offshore engine gives the name a clear growth thread distinct from the mature fields that make up much of the sector. As crude firmed this week, the scale and low cost of the Guyana barrels drew particular attention, since they feed directly into how the market reads the group's expanding production footprint. Alongside its offshore reach, the group holds a deep position in the Permian basin, the vast shale region straddling the American Southwest that has become the engine of domestic oil growth. A large acreage base there feeds a steady stream of barrels that the group can dial up or down with relative speed compared with long-cycle offshore projects. Shale output answers to drilling that can be ramped quickly, giving the group a flexible lever to lean into firmer crude. The Permian barrels sit close to the group's refining and chemical plants along the coast, a proximity that trims transport and knits the upstream and downstream arms more tightly together. After royalty and cost recovery, which is capped at 75% of production, the remaining oil is shared 50-50 with the government of Guyana.                                        My Trusted Source The move in crude dominated energy trading. After climbing steeply on worries that global supply could tighten, benchmark prices drifted lower as those fears cooled and the market weighed fresh barrels coming onto the scene. For an integrated group, a softer crude price cuts both ways. While crude slipped, refining margins stayed firm, a detail that mattered for the downstream business. Refining spreads measure the difference between the cost of crude fed into a plant and the value of the gasoline, diesel and jet fuel that come out. When those spreads stay healthy even as crude eases, the refining arm can lean into the gap. Firm margins across the refining slate help steady group-wide earnings during stretches when crude prices wobble, and that cushioning effect is a core reason the integrated model has stayed in favor through many cycles in the oil and gas sector. An integrated energy group knits together activities that are often split across separate companies. title: Why Did XOM, CVX, MPC Stocks Surge To 52-Week Highs Today? - TradingView
content: Shares of energy companies Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM), Chevron Corp. (CVX), and Marathon Petroleum Corp. (MPC) surged to annual highs on Monday as oil prices rallied amid growing geopolitical tensions. Brent crude prices touched nearly $110 a barrel on Monday as tensions in the Middle East continued to ratchet up. A series of recent escalations, including attacks on commercial ships near the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi missile strikes on Saudi Arabia, and Ukraine’s strike on a Russian refinery, stoked fears about a further constraint in fuel supplies, sending prices higher. Worries continued despite the U.S. government’s efforts to curtail rising prices, including planned fuel releases and changes to U.S. sanctions on Russian imported fuel. Since the U.S.-Iran war began in February, energy prices have been climbing steadily, boosting energy companies. As per Koyfin data, energy stocks have outperformed the S&P 500 by a significant margin in 2026. Exxon Mobil, Chevron, and Marathon Petroleum shares surged to 52-week highs on Monday before closing lower amid the steep climb in oil prices. XOM stock hit an annual high of $179.30 during trading hours on Monday before closing about 0.4% down. CVX stock surged to a 52-week high of $225.67, but ended the session 0.28% lower. MPC stock rallied to a 52-week high of $493.98 during regular trading, but finished the day nearly 1% down. Retail sentiment around XOM, CVX and MPC stocks was ‘bullish’ at the time of writing on Stocktwits. content: Which of these integrated energy giants is a better investment right now? Chevron (CVX +0.47%) and ExxonMobil (XOM +0.13%) are two of the world's largest integrated energy companies. They both own upstream exploration and extraction businesses, midstream pipelines, and downstream refineries. Over the past 12 months, Chevron's stock has rallied 45% while ExxonMobil's stock has risen 58%. Both stocks benefited from rising oil prices, but which stock is the better buy right now? Chevron is smaller than ExxonMobil, but both companies generate most of their revenue from their upstream businesses. However, Chevron generates more of its profits (about 80%) from its upstream business than ExxonMobil (about 70%). That's because ExxonMobil operates a larger downstream business -- which acts as a secondary profit engine -- than Chevron. ExxonMobil's downstream business produces a lot of petrochemicals, while Chevron's downstream business has minimal exposure to that market. When crude oil prices rise, upstream businesses typically grow their revenues faster than their expenses. However, downstream businesses often struggle as their input costs rise. When crude oil prices decline, upstream businesses struggle, but downstream businesses fare better -- as long as the crack spread (between crude oil costs and retail fuel prices) remains stable. Therefore, Chevron's streamlined, upstream-heavy business model makes it a more attractive investment than ExxonMobil when oil prices spike. But when oil prices pull back, ExxonMobil's scale and downstream diversification could make it a more compelling investment. Missed Nvidia in 2009? Both companies plan to increase their oil and gas production by about 3% annually through the end of the decade. Chevron pays a forward yield of 3.2%, while ExxonMobil pays a lower forward yield of 2.3%. Chevron has raised its dividend annually for 39 consecutive years, while ExxonMobil has maintained that streak for 43 years. If they reach 50 years, they'll become Dividend Kings. Both companies have plenty of room to raise their dividends. Over the past 12 months, Chevron and ExxonMobil had payout ratios of 67% and 53%, respectively. In 2025, Chevron's EPS dropped 32% as crude oil prices declined, its refining margins shrank, and it finalized its acquisition of Hess Corporation. But from 2025 to 2028, analysts expect its EPS to grow at a 26% CAGR as it expands in Guyana (one of the world's fastest-growing oil regions) by integrating Hess' assets; produces more oil in the Permian Basin and Kazakhstan, and accelerates its deepwater projects. Yet its stock still trades at 15 times next year's earnings. In 2025, ExxonMobil's EPS dipped 15% as it faced some of the same headwinds as Chevron and divested its weaker assets. But from 2025 to 2028, analysts expect its EPS to grow at a 20% CAGR as it integrates its recent acquisition of Pioneer Natural Resources (which expanded its reach in the Permian Basin), increases its production in Guyana, and prioritizes the production of higher-margin chemical performance products and specialized fuels at its downstream business. Its stock also trades at 15 times next year's earnings. Chevron and ExxonMobil both look fundamentally cheap because they're valued as cyclical commodity stocks rather than higher-growth energy plays. However, they're both still solid long-term investments for investors who can stomach the short-term fluctuations in oil prices. But if I could only pick one, I'd choose Chevron over ExxonMobil for three simple reasons: it has more exposure to rising oil prices, it's growing faster, and it pays a higher dividend. ExxonMobil’s dividend looks built to last, but a modest yield and a valuation that leaves little room for error could put its total-return appeal to the test. ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation (NYSE:XOM) has a set of advantages that most smaller oil companies can only dream of. Its business stretches across exploration, production, refining, chemicals, and specialty products. This means ExxonMobil can make money at every step of the energy chain, instead of relying only on the ups and downs of crude oil prices. What really sets ExxonMobil apart are three things: its massive scale, the way it ties all its operations together, and the valuable assets it owns. Big projects in Guyana’s deepwater fields and the Permian Basin let ExxonMobil boost production at a good price. Its vast refining network, in-house technology, and worldwide logistics make the company extra efficient, something newcomers can’t easily copy. Plus, its strong balance sheet and easy access to capital mean it can take on big projects that might take years before they pay off. That combination of scale and income potential also makes it worth comparing with other established dividend payers featured in Top 10 Unstoppable Dividend Stocks to Buy. Still, even with all these advantages, ExxonMobil isn’t immune to trouble. When oil prices drop, the whole business feels it. There’s always the risk that huge investments or new environmental rules could eat into profits. Also read: 10 Best Battery Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation is trading at a forward P/E of 14.77, compared to a trailing P/E of 20.75. That difference shows analysts think earnings are set to climb, which equates to a forward earnings yield of about 6.8%. That’s a fair valuation for a company as large as ExxonMobil, but it’s not exactly cheap. Just a few months ago, its forward P/E was 12.08. For comparison, Chevron is currently trading at a forward multiple of around 15.20. The big question is whether ExxonMobil’s growth and improved efficiency can really justify this higher price. And with the 10-year Treasury yield recently moving above 5%, the extra return you get from ExxonMobil isn’t that much higher, so investors are not being paid a big premium for taking on the risks of the oil business. ExxonMobil’s next earnings report comes out on October 30, 2026. Also take a look at: BP (BP) vs Exxon Mobil (XOM): Which Oil Major is a Better Buy? ExxonMobil’s dividend is known more for its reliability than for a big payout. The company pays an annual dividend of $4.12 per share, which works out to a 2.30% yield and a payout ratio of 52.51%. That yield is a lot lower than its five-year average of 3.38%, meaning the stock price has grown faster than the dividend itself. Even then, the stock stands out among other dividend stocks gaining this year, because of its Dividend Aristocrat status. The payout ratio gives ExxonMobil a decent buffer if earnings dip, but it’s not the whole picture for a big oil company. Dividends only work if there’s enough cash left after running the business, paying taxes, and investing in new projects. In the first half of 2026, ExxonMobil paid out $8.6 billion in dividends. Its most recent report also showed a conservative net-debt-to-capital ratio of 10.7% as of June, which means the company has the flexibility to keep paying dividends even if times get tough. ExxonMobil also has an impressive history of raising its dividend. As of January 2026, it’s boosted its annual dividend per share for 43 straight years, including a 4% bump in the fourth quarter of 2025. That kind of track record matters, since growing dividends help investors keep up with inflation and boost their returns on what they originally paid. Of course, just because the company’s raised its dividend in the past doesn’t mean it always will, especially if oil prices fall or big spending needs pop up. But there’s more to owning ExxonMobil than just the dividend. The total return, meaning the combination of dividends, share buybacks, and price appreciation, matters a lot. In 2025, ExxonMobil returned $37.2 billion to shareholders, split between $17.2 billion in dividends and $20 billion in buybacks. Buybacks can help boost earnings per share, but they’re not guaranteed. How much the company buys back depends on cash flow and what’s happening in the market. With a 2.30% yield, ExxonMobil isn’t paying out as much as it has in the past. The dividend looks safe for now, but the stock price doesn’t leave much of a cushion if oil prices take a hit. The stock is a better fit for investors looking for steady, long-term growth and rising income, rather than those chasing a high yield right away. ExxonMobil’s strengths, including its competitive edge, valuable assets, and integrated approach, help support a reliable dividend. But with the stock price climbing lately, there’s less of a safety net for new investors. The shares make the most sense for people who want steady, long-term exposure to the energy sector and a dividend that can grow over time, not just for those looking for a quick boost in income. ExxonMobil reported that improved refining margins could contribute approximately to third-quarter earnings compared with the preceding quarter. Refining margins represent the difference between the value of refined petroleum products and the cost of the crude oil and other inputs used to produce them. Margins can change with fuel demand, refinery utilisation, crude supply, maintenance schedules and regional differences in product availability. The Energy Products business processes crude oil into fuels and other petroleum products used in transportation, industrial operations and commercial markets. Its performance therefore depends on both feedstock costs and the prices received for refined products. When refined-product markets strengthen relative to crude costs, refining operations can contribute more substantially to segment earnings. The reported development also illustrates the importance of geographical and operational flexibility across an extensive refining network. However, refining conditions can change quickly as supply availability, demand patterns and refinery operations evolve. While refining margins have strengthened, upstream operations face pressure from lower liquids prices. The upstream business encompasses exploration, development and production of crude oil and natural gas. Revenue and earnings from these activities depend on commodity prices, production volumes, operating expenses and the characteristics of individual assets. ExxonMobil maintains significant upstream operations in regions including Guyana and the Permian Basin. Guyana has become an important source of offshore production, while the Permian Basin represents a substantial position in United States shale oil and natural gas development. Production growth from established projects can affect the companys overall operating mix. However, the financial contribution of additional production also depends on commodity prices, project costs, infrastructure availability and operating performance. The companys integrated structure means stronger downstream conditions can partly offset weaker upstream results during certain periods. The extent of that offset varies according to the relative size of segment earnings and the duration of changes in commodity and refined-product markets. ExxonMobil also operates chemical manufacturing and specialty products businesses. Chemical Products supplies materials used in packaging, construction, automotive manufacturing, industrial applications and consumer goods. Specialty Products includes lubricants, finished fluids and other performance-oriented materials used across transportation and industrial markets. These businesses respond to different demand drivers from those affecting crude oil production and refining. Chemical earnings can depend on manufacturing demand, product spreads, plant utilisation and feedstock costs. Specialty products are influenced by industrial activity, customer requirements and demand for materials designed for specific operating conditions. Disruptions can affect crude availability and refined-product margins differently, depending on the location of assets and the products involved. title: Why Did XOM, V, TEAM Stocks Hit 52-Week Highs Last Week? - Stocktwits
content: Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM), Visa Inc. (V) and Atlassian Corp. (TEAM) climbed to new 52-week highs on Friday as developments in energy refining, international payments and enterprise software attracted investor attention, while analyst optimism and new product capabilities added to the positive outlook for the companies. Exxon Mobil and Visa stocks climbed 2% and 0.7%, while Atlassian pared gains and ended the session 4% lower. Exxon Mobil stock hit a record high of $179.16 after a regulatory filing suggested improved refining conditions could boost third-quarter (Q3) results. The company estimated that stronger margins in its Energy Products business would add about $4.5 billion compared with the previous quarter. Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta estimated that the disclosure pointed to earnings per share of around $4.10, above FactSet's consensus forecast of $3.87. However, the outlook still remained below Goldman Sachs' own $4.33 estimate. Investors are awaiting the company's Q3 report, scheduled for Oct. 30. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock improved to ‘bullish’ from ‘neutral’. Visa stock extended its advance, hitting a record high of $404.74 as investors reacted to the launch of the company’s stablecoin payment service. The service lets banks and payment companies send money overseas faster using Circle’s USD Coin (USDC). TD Cowen analysts said stablecoins could work alongside existing payment systems rather than replace them. BMO Capital raised Visa’s price target to $425 from $405 and maintained an ‘Outperform’ rating. The firm sees strong consumer spending and expects Visa’s revenue and earnings growth to remain strong. BMO added that growth in additional services and newer payment businesses could help offset slower growth in Visa’s core business. Retail sentiment around the stock slipped to ‘bullish’ from ‘extremely bullish’. Atlassian stock hit a new annual high of $223.70, driven by strong demand and more customers moving to its cloud services as the company shifts customers from legacy Data Center licenses to cloud-based Jira and Confluence subscriptions. Last week, Mizuho analyst Gregg Moskowitz raised his price target to $235 from $215 and maintained an ‘Outperform’ rating. He cited healthy feedback from industry contacts, solid cloud usage and continued interest in AI tools. Wells Fargo analyst Ryan MacWilliams lifted his target to $230 from $180 and retained an ‘Overweight’ rating. The analyst said larger corporate customers were moving from Data Center products to cloud subscriptions while retaining their existing user bases. MacWilliams also pointed to growing early interest in Rovo, Atlassian's AI assistant. Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘bearish’. So far this year, XOM, V and TEAM stocks have gained between 14%  and 48%. The biotech spotlight will move from kidney cancer to Huntington’s disease and personalized cancer treatment this week, as Arcus Biosciences (RCUS), Alnylam (ALNY), Moderna (MRNA) and Merck (MRK) deliver clinical updates amid a busy schedule of earnings and medical conferences. The Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLV) gained 3% last week, outperforming the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY), which fell 2%, and the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), down 6%. The iShares Biotechnology ETF (IBB) declined 2.2%, trailing SPY but holding up better than QQQ, while the SPDR S&P Biotech ETF (XBI) dropped 6%. Arcus Biosciences (RCUS) will present kidney-cancer findings on Tuesday from its ARC-20 study of Casdatifan. The update covers initial treatment combinations: Casdatifan plus Cabozantinib in 43 previously treated patients, and Casdatifan alone in 121 more heavily treated patients. Median follow-up is about 21 months for the Cabozantinib combination and 28 months for Casdatifan alone. Achieve Life Sciences (ACHV) will present year-long Cytisinicline findings on Tuesday at CHEST in Phoenix. The ORCA-OL study enrolled 475 adults who smoked or vaped and received the drug alongside behavioral support. Results include lab-confirmed measures of quitting. Achieve plans to resubmit its smoking-cessation application in the fourth quarter after a June FDA rejection that the company said concerned manufacturing and labeling, with no clinical efficacy or safety deficiencies identified. Eupraxia Pharmaceuticals (EPRX) will present on Monday at UEG Week in Barcelona on tissue changes following EP-104GI treatment for eosinophilic esophagitis, an inflammatory condition that can make swallowing difficult. The findings come from the early, open-label Resolve study, while interim results from its randomized Phase 2b portion are expected in December. RegenXBio (RGNX) will review its sura-vec treatment for wet age-related macular degeneration at a Tuesday investor event ahead of trial results expected in the fourth quarter. Roche (RHHBY) will report third-quarter sales on Thursday. First-half sales grew 6%, excluding currency effects but fell 2% in Swiss francs. Growth was led by Xolair, Hemlibra, Ocrevus, Phesgo and Vabysmo. Argenx (ARGX) also reported on Thursday, following positive Phase 2 findings for its celiac-disease treatment FB102 and its decision to stop its Phase 3 Sjogren’s disease trial after an interim analysis indicated it was unlikely to succeed. Abbott (ABT), Danaher (DHR) and Thermo Fisher Scientific (TMO) report on Wednesday. TG Therapeutics (TGTX) will present its first Phase 1 Azer-cel results in primary progressive multiple sclerosis (MS) on Friday at MSToronto2026, with the full abstract due Wednesday. The treatment uses genetically modified donor immune cells. Other presentations cover seven-year Briumvi outcomes, findings from routine care and a simplified initial dosing schedule. Kyverna Therapeutics (KYTX) will present one-year Phase 2 Kysa-8 findings for miv-cel in stiff person syndrome on Wednesday, followed by updated results from a physician-led Phase 1 study in progressive MS on Friday. Immunic (IMUX) will share longer-term progressive-MS findings from Calliper on  Wednesday. Zenas BioPharma (ZBIO) follows on Thursday with Phase 2 MS findings for Obexelimab and Orelabrutinib. Alnylam Pharmaceuticals (ALNY) will present initial Phase 1 ALN-HTT02 results on Friday at the European Huntington’s Disease Network congress in Krakow. Developed with Regeneron, the investigational RNA-interference treatment targets huntingtin, the protein implicated in Huntington’s disease. Tango Therapeutics (TNGX) will hold a pancreatic-cancer webcast on Friday discussing Vopimetostat combined with Daraxonrasib or Zoldonrasib. The study involves patients with MTAP-deleted, RAS-mutant cancers. Humacyte (HUMA) will present interim Phase 3 V012 results on Thursday, comparing its tissue-engineered vessel with a conventional fistula for dialysis access in women with end-stage kidney disease. The company targets a supplemental FDA application this quarter. Vera Therapeutics (VERA) will present its Origin 3 final efficacy analysis on Thursday, following the September announcement of the results. Saturday brings separate interim Phase 2 Pioneer findings in IgA nephropathy and primary membranous nephropathy. Maze Therapeutics (MAZE) presents additional detail from its previously reported Phase 2 Horizon kidney-disease study on Saturday. Climb Bio (CLYM) presents healthy-volunteer CLYM116 findings on Thursday and preliminary Phase 2 Budoprutug results in primary membranous nephropathy on Saturday. ESMO opens on Friday in Madrid. Moderna (MRNA) and Merck (MRK) will present Phase 3 INTerpath-001 melanoma findings on Saturday, testing individualized treatment intismeran autogene plus Keytruda against Keytruda alone after surgery. The companies previously announced improvements in recurrence-free and distant-metastasis-free survival. Overall-survival evaluation continues. Moderna will also host an investor webcast on Saturday. Compass Therapeutics (CMPX) presents Companion-002 findings on Saturday. Tovecimig plus Paclitaxel improved response rates and progression-free survival in previously treated biliary tract cancer, but did not demonstrate a statistically significant overall-survival benefit. Compass says the FDA recommended another trial demonstrating a survival benefit before an application. Immatics (IMTX) presents IMA203CD8 cell-therapy findings on Friday, followed Saturday by IMA402 bispecific data and Anzu-cel melanoma follow-up. Biohaven (BHVN), Perspective Therapeutics (CATX) and Eikon Therapeutics (EIKN) also have early-stage cancer presentations on Friday. Additional presentations include Incyte’s (INCY) CDK2-inhibitor findings on Friday and colorectal-cancer bispecific data on Saturday, alongside Regeneron’s (REGN) final Phase 2 analysis of Cemiplimab before surgery in cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma on Saturday. Shares of neocloud operators rose over the weekend after a week in the market driven by concerns over the sustainability of their business models and macro triggers such as a higher-than-expected inflation reading. CoreWeave (CRWV) stock rose 2.6% in overnight trading late Sunday, while Nebius (NBIS) rose 3.8% and IREN gained 3.3%. CoreWeave shares fell over 20% from Monday through Wednesday, before gaining 6% on Thursday on support from Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang. The slide mirrored declines across the neocloud sector, including Nebius NBIS and IREN. Investor sentiment toward AI infrastructure stocks, spanning semiconductor makers and cloud providers, has weakened amid higher financing costs and growing doubts about how quickly the technology will deliver returns. Industry executives expect only seven to 10 of hundreds of neoclouds to survive, with Nvidia supporting them through easier credit terms, site selection, and $20 billion in leases, according to a report in The Information published Sunday. The selloff has spread to other parts of the market. Data center operator and cloud firm Nscale is reportedly facing opposition to the $30 billion valuation it seeks for its IPO, Bloomberg reported Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter. A group of investors has recently urged that a valuation in the $16 billion to $19 billion range would be more likely to appeal to buyers. The report came after Microsoft, one of the company’s biggest customers, pulled out of a UK data center deal after the site faced delays due to power constraints. Bloomberg reported last Wednesday that CoreWeave’s unsecured debt due in 2032 fell below 80 cents on the dollar, a level widely seen as the threshold for financial strain. Meanwhile, research firm Gartner issued a report saying it expects 80% of neocloud operators to not survive by 2030, sparking panic across the sector. Tech investor Chamath Palihapitiya, founder of investment firm Social Capital, called out CoreWeave’s soaring yields on X late Tuesday. Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk responded, “yikes.” CoreWeave’s CEO Mike Intrator reportedly told staff the market is acting “irrationally” and that he remains confident in the AI cloud company’s business model, with several analysts supporting that view. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment for CRWV, NBIS and IREN climbed sharply over the past week and was ‘extremely bullish’ as of late Sunday. The market may be overstating CoreWeave’s debt and financing risks while overlooking its sizable backlog, operating scale and customer prepayments on roughly 70% of recent deals, a retail trader said. “Does CRWV have debt? Absolutely. Is the capital structure something to watch closely? Absolutely. But there’s a big difference between ‘highly leveraged’ and ‘business is failing.’ Jensen Huang says CRWV’s cost of capital is actually decreasing, Cantor calls this one of the best entry opportunities, and now Truist is pushing back on the financing panic,” they said. Among the neocloud group, traders seemed most optimistic about Nebius. “$NBIS All should be good! I will double my position now. As I said before, I believe this will recover faster than any other beaten-down AI stock. The FUD is way overdone,” a trader posted. Year to date, CRWV is now down 14.3%, while IREN is down 28.5%. NBIS is up 98%. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. Shares of Tesla, Inc. (TSLA) rose 1% overnight late Sunday as CEO Elon Musk put the Optimus humanoid robot and Cybercab robotaxi at the center of the company’s future value, while a Morningstar analyst said that its “flying” Roadster could draw buyers to the wider Tesla lineup. TSLA stock fell 7% last week, logging its worst week in nearly three months. Musk’s remarks came after the recent unveiling of the long-awaited sports car, which briefly flew and flipped using cold-gas thrusters during autonomous demos, drawing praise for Tesla’s engineering and also questions about the vehicle’s practicality. “Optimus and Cybercab will be the vast majority of Tesla’s value,” Musk said on X. He said superintelligence, robots, solar power and transporting mass into space were the businesses capable of reaching extraordinary economic scale, with progress in the first two enabling the others. “But Roadster is super cool, so we’re doing it anyway,” he added. Meanwhile, Morningstar sees the Roadster as a “halo car” that showcases Tesla’s best engineering and could stimulate demand across its vehicle lineup. “A high-end sports car that is the fastest car in the world and that can temporarily fly does a great job highlighting Tesla as a unique luxury car company, which should draw consumers to Tesla vehicles and could support increased deliveries once the car enters production in 2028,” Morningstar said. The firm said Tesla’s claimed 0-to-60 mph time of 0.81 seconds, if recorded at a racetrack, would be less than half the current 1.66-second record. Morningstar forecasts fewer than 2,000 annual Roadster deliveries after production ramps up, making it Tesla’s lowest-volume vehicle. Chris Camillo, an investor and author of Laughing at Wall Street, saw a bigger payoff in Musk’s willingness to risk a public failure.  “Almost no CEO would willingly expose their company to that kind of public humiliation for a product with so little financial upside. Elon did,” Camillo said on X. He said that Musk was helping revive America’s appetite for pursuing seemingly impossible ideas, with an influence on future founders that could dwarf anything Tesla sells. “Whether the Roadster ever makes Tesla a dollar or impacts $TSLA stock price is almost beside the point,” he said. “We need more people willing to risk failure in pursuit of things the rest of us think are impossible. Because when they succeed we all win.” Camillo, who said he had been both bullish and critical of Tesla, also questioned the impulse to turn the demonstration into an argument over whether it qualified as a flying car. “Can we just acknowledge how insanely cool that moment was?” he added. Musk’s posts over the weekend raised expectations beyond the demo last week. “I think we can reach a peak speed of >0.5 Mach or ~400 mph,” he said, exceeding the top speed of 230 mph. He also claimed that the Roadster has an advantage over Formula 1 cars. “Even without rocket thrusters, Roadster will crush the best Formula 1 track times, because we are using suction and active control surfaces, both of which are banned by F1,” Musk said. “The Roadster could fly, rotate and stick to the underside of an overpass like Spider-Man,” he said in another post. Musk also said owners would be able to request the demo tricks autonomously and promised a looping test track at Tesla’s Texas headquarters “crazier even than Hot Wheels.” Musk fired back at Yann LeCun, the Turing Award-winning researcher often called an “AI godfather,” after he dismissed Tesla’s flying Roadster demo as impractical. “I fart in your general direction,” Musk replied. LeCun questioned the compressed-air system’s efficiency, estimating that even if air accounted for half the car’s mass, it would provide less than 10 seconds of useful thrust. “Probably more like 5 seconds, actually,” he said, arguing that the vehicle would need to be a lightweight shell containing large air tanks. “Cute demo, but totally impractical. But of course, you knew that,” LeCun added. Tesla lists two-seat Performance and Thrust versions, requiring reservation payments of $50,000 and $250,000, respectively, plus an invitation-only, single-seat Rocket variant with perimeter thrusters. Reservations secure a place in line, with no delivery guarantee. The vehicle is not approved for public road use, and availability depends on regional laws. Musk acknowledged safety limitations and uncertainty over its legality everywhere. Tesla reports third-quarter earnings on Wednesday. Morningstar expects investors to focus on robotaxi and humanoid-robot updates, alongside free cash flow, which it forecasts will remain negative for a second straight quarter. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for TSLA slipped to ‘neutral’ from ‘bullish’ levels a day ago amid ‘high’ message volume. One user said, “$TSLA all of you bearish gooners don't understand that $TSLA will fly just like the roadster on Monday!!” Another user said, “$TSLA legally, if a buyout is going to happen, it's likely to happen during their next ER [earnings report], which is scheduled to happen on October 21.  Are you ready to launch? $500.” So far this year, Tesla's stock has lagged its "Magnificent Seven" peers, making it the group's worst performer, down about 21%. Last week brought a mix of strong product demand, corporate restructuring, insider buying, and development setbacks for five companies in the spotlight. Apple Inc. (AAPL) attracted attention with its first foldable iPhone, Netflix Inc. (NFLX) announced job cuts, GameStop Corp. (GME) saw continued insider purchases, Tesla Inc. (TSLA) showcased its redesigned Roadster, and Rocket Lab Corp. (RKLB) pushed its Neutron rocket debut into 2027. Apple's new iPhone Duo quickly built a long preorder backlog after orders opened Oct. 16. Delivery estimates for the $1,999 foldable smartphone slipped into January 2027, raising expectations while leaving questions about supply.  Evercore ISI viewed the 100-day waiting period as a positive sign for Apple, saying demand has started strongly. Bloomberg Intelligence analysts suggested sales could exceed their earlier fiscal 2027 estimate of 14 million units and $28 billion in revenue. Separately, Apple and Meta Platforms Inc. (META) announced work to help developers run Meta's Muse Spark model on Mac Studio computers, highlighting a new area of cooperation between the longtime rivals. Users can connect two to four computers to run AI tasks locally, which may improve privacy and reduce cloud costs. Apple stock rose 2% over the week. However, on Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘extremely bearish’. Netflix stock edged up 0.3% over the week as the company devised plans to cut about 1,000 jobs, or 6% of its workforce. The cuts will mainly affect product, technology, legal and human resources teams. Co-CEOs Greg Peters and Ted Sarandos said Netflix remains on track to meet its yearly financial targets. However, the company faces challenges in keeping viewers engaged and competing for audiences as it expands into live programming and other formats. Also, Netflix named former Disney and Fox executive Peter Rice as its new chief content officer, replacing Bela Bajaria, who is leaving after nearly 10 years. He will oversee TV shows, movies and live events. Retail sentiment around the stock turned ‘bearish’ from ‘neutral’. GameStop remained in the spotlight as CEO Ryan Cohen continued buying company shares as part of a buying spree that began in September. Last week, he bought 844,130 shares worth about $22.8 million. Over the past two months, total insider purchases totaled about $99 million, boosting investor confidence. GameStop stock posted its seventh green week, up nearly 1%. Retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘bullish’. Tesla unveiled its long-awaited revamped Roadster prototype in Texas, featuring SpaceX-developed thrusters (SPCX). The company said the car could go from zero to 60 mph in less than a second. Production is planned for 2028, but the rocket-thruster version is not approved for public roads. On Sunday, CEO Elon Musk said in an X post that the Optimus humanoid robot and Cybercab robotaxi will make up most of the company’s value in the future, highlighting AI and robotics as key growth drivers beyond electric cars. Despite the optimism, Tesla stock fell 7.3% this week. Tesla will report its third-quarter results on Oct. 21. According to Fiscal.ai, analysts expect earnings of $0.45 per share and revenue of $28.1 billion. Retail sentiment around the stock turned ‘neutral’ from ‘bullish’. Rocket Lab stock plunged over 25% to its worst week ever as the company postponed the first flight of its partially reusable Neutron rocket after identifying manufacturing problems involving carbon-fiber components in the vehicle's propellant tanks. CEO Peter Beck said the company had adjusted its manufacturing process and would complete further inspections and testing before setting a launch date. The delay creates another hurdle for Rocket Lab as it works to expand beyond its smaller Electron rocket and compete for larger launch contracts. The update drew a slew of price target cuts across Wall Street. On Friday, Citizens lowered its price target for Rocket Lab from $130 to $90 but kept its ‘Outperform’ rating. The firm said Rocket Lab has tested a manufacturing fix and is rebuilding the affected part, putting safety ahead of speed and added that the delay could also affect the company’s ability to earn money from Neutron launches in 2027 and 2028. So far this year, AAPL and GME stocks gained 26% and 33%, respectively, while NFLX, TSLA, and RKLB stocks declined 21% to 27%. Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. Ethereum (ETH) was wrong with its “world computer” idea, Cardano (ADA) founder Charles Hoskinson said. He suggested using Midnight (NIGHT),, the privacy network developed alongside Cardano, as the solution. He described Midnight’s approach as “What they got wrong with this idea of one giant shared world computer. Computers are personal,” he said. Public blockchains reveal too much of their users, Hoskinson said. He asked whether people want everyone to see “what you buy, who you talk to,” forever. That problem grew as AI agents continued to proliferate. Personal data was needed for it to be useful, he said. He said he was not comfortable sharing that data with Sam Altman, the CEO of OpenAI, or Dario Amodei, the CEO of Anthropic. He called his answer a “night frame,” his personal computing box built on Midnight. It employs three tools. Zero-knowledge proofs verified the validity of an outcome without revealing the details. Multi-party computation allowed multiple parties to compute on data without revealing their inputs. Trusted execution environments ran code in a sealed portion of a chip. Hoskinson summed up the design simply. “What goes in, no one else can see,” he said. Midnight City will be fully operational “in the next few months,” said Hoskinson. It will be a simulated world where AI agents live, trade, and test each other. It already has about 14,000 beta testers, he said. Users will be able to host an agent with its own wallet and identity,” he said. That agent could rent a trading strategy developed by somebody else. The marketplace will reach Solana (SOL), Ethereum (ETH), Hyperliquid (HYPE), and Binance (BNB), Hoskinson said. He said crypto might still chase small improvements in speed and fees, or it could "hand control of this industry back to Wall Street, have them run all the nodes.” He called on builders to show the world “what a crypto-native civilization would look like.” He also downplayed rivalries among chains and said users shouldn’t have to worry about which network settles their transactions. However, all three tokens were struggling. Midnight’s price was trading around $0.0401, down 19.3% over the past week. Cardano’s price dropped 13.1% during that period to about $0.2158. Ethereum’s price, meanwhile, dropped 6.7% this week to around $2,372. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around NIGHT and ADA remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while the retail sentiment around ETH stayed in the ‘extremely bearish’ zone over the past day.
